title: Nano-structural analysis of zein-cellulose derivative composite films using AFM-Lorentz contact resonance and local thermal analyses
content: This study investigated nanoscale zein particle suspensions (ZPS) prepared from aqueous ethanol (90% w/w) by antisolvent precipitation. The zein particles had a volume-based median particle diameter (Dv50) of 0.208 as determined by light scattering. The ZPS was incorporated into either an ethanol-soluble ethyl cellulose (EC, 4% w/w) solution or a water-soluble hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC, 4% w/w) solution to form continuous composite films by casting. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) revealed distinct particle distributions and morphologies in the two polymer matrices. SEM images showed a bilayer structure in the zein-HPMC film. In contrast, in the zein-EC film, the particles were dispersed throughout the cross-section, with an increased concentration towards the casting substrate. AFM in Lorentz contact resonance mode revealed two distinct stiffness regions in the zein-EC film, whereas only one phase was observed in the zein-HPMC film. Nano-thermal analysis detected two local softening temperatures in the zein-EC film, whereas only one temperature was detected in the zein-HPMC film. In summary, this study reports a method to prepare EC and HPMC microcomposites with controlled zein particle distribution and a distinct morphology, resulting from matrix-dependent zein-polymer interactions. These structural differences may provide a basis for tailoring the localization and mobility of active compounds in functional food films and packaging, although their potential effects on bioactive delivery performance require further validation.
